issues.description: The problem statement and template imply single-argument constructors that initialize an Animal's name (UML shows only 'name' and the commented example in Main uses new Seal("Clarabelle") etc.), but the solution introduces an additional 'age' attribute and requires two-argument constructors (String name, int age) for Animal and all concrete animals. This discrepancy between the expected constructor signatures will confuse students (and cause mismatches if they follow the template/example) and makes the solution structurally different from the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor expectations consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML and template Main to include an 'age' attribute and show two-argument constructors for Animal and its subclasses, or (B) remove the 'age' attribute from the solution and change the solution constructors to single-argument constructors (String name) so they match the UML and the example usage in the template. Ensure all related classes (Seal, Pig, Goat) and their constructors/signatures are adjusted accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and the provided template example instantiate animals with a single String parameter (name), implying constructors initialize only the 'name' attribute. The solution, however, introduces an additional 'age' attribute in Animal and uses two-argument constructors (String name, int age) for Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat. This mismatch in the constructor signature (and the extra 'age' attribute) creates a mapping/confusion for students: the example code in Main and the UML/problem text imply one-argument constructors while the solution's classes require two arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent across artifacts. Either (A) remove the added 'age' attribute from the solution and use single-argument constructors (String name) for Animal and subclasses to match the UML/problem and template Main example, or (B) update the problem statement, UML, and template example to include the 'age' attribute and show two-argument constructors (String name, int age) everywhere (including updating the commented Main instantiations). Ensure constructors in Seal, Pig, and Goat consistently match the canonical signature chosen.
